key_insight: MedMLX adapts 21 established medical imaging AI models to Apple Silicon, closely matching original software outputs without requiring NVIDIA hardware.
clinical_relevance: Local organ and tumor segmentation could broaden access to cancer imaging research tools, but this study does not establish clinical benefit or address drug discovery.
method: Reimplemented 21 imaging models in Apple's MLX framework.
Compared outputs with original software on Intel CPU and NVIDIA GPU using 11 public imaging datasets.
Measured memory use and processing time on an M1 Max with 64 GB memory.
evidence_signal: MedMLX matched 211 of 212 comparisons; segmentation agreement required Dice ≥0.99 for every label, and 19 models used under 16 GB with a memory-saving setting.
watch_item: Output agreement is not clinical validation; performance testing used one hardware configuration, and memory savings increased processing time by a median of 13%.
paper_title: MedMLX: On-Device Medical Imaging AI for Apple Silicon
